key_idea: Low-energy states give measurement distributions that sit on approximate codewords; code expansion forces those codewords into well-separated clusters; and an X/Z uncertainty principle together with the constant rate keeps at least one basis from concentrating on a single cluster, which then gives the log-depth lower bound.
reason: The argument runs along one clean line: support on approximate codewords, then clustering from expansion, then uncertainty ruling out concentration, then spread implying depth. Playing the two conjugate bases against each other to get spread from the code rate is a striking move. Some bookkeeping with constants and the reliance on outside expansion theorems for good qLDPC codes keep it below book-proof level.
recognized: Anshu–Breuckmann–Nirkhe, 'NLTS Hamiltonians from good quantum codes' (2022)
